attempts.summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 for SSH key-only access: created the user, installed the specified ed25519 public key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct permissions, locked the account password, and enforced key-based SSH authentication cluster-wide via /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf (PasswordAuthentication no, PubkeyAuthentication yes, PermitEmptyPasswords no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no). Also had to generate missing SSH host keys and fix the missing /run/sshd privilege-separation directory (added a systemd-tmpfiles rule so it persists across reboots) since sshd was not actually running beforehand. Verified end-to-end with real SSH logins (password auth rejected, pubkey auth succeeds). Completed the mandatory node1 restart-evidence protocol: captured baseline boot_id and service state, issued a native reboot, polled until the node returned, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd, opsadmin, the authorized key, and functional key-based login all recovered correctly post-reboot.
